rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding ~4 at.% Hf to a W38Ta36Cr15V11 alloy, whereas the hidden target varied V from 0 to 3 and 5 at.% in W–Ta alloys. Both are compositional modifications, but the specific element (Hf vs. V) and the base alloy system (W–Ta–Cr–V vs. W–Ta) are different, making this a different specific lever.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies irradiation up to 8 dpa at 300–600°C, while the hidden target used 1 MeV Kr ions to ~20 dpa at 1073 K (800°C). Both involve energetic-particle irradiation at elevated temperature, but the dose, temperature range, and ion type differ substantially.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes Hf segregation to grain boundaries binding Cr and V to suppress precipitate nucleation. The hidden target's mechanism relies on V-induced changes in chemical short-range order and defect mobility to enhance recombination and suppress segregation/voids. These are different mechanistic pathways.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts suppression of Cr-V precipitates and low hardening, while the hidden target predicts reduced void size/density, less segregation, and retained nanocrystalline structure. Both predict improved radiation tolerance, but the specific property (precipitate suppression vs. void/segregation reduction) and the baseline alloy differ.
